referenceName: SERHANT: cinematic media and multi-market brokerage

source.name: SERHANT. official website
source.sourceType: official direct real estate brokerage website captured in Playwright Chromium
source.rightsEvidence: Requester-attested clearance dated 2026-09-29 covers internal desktop and mobile screenshot retention, derived design prompts, and pipeline-model reference use. No source-owner grant was supplied or independently verified.

referenceDna.annotatedDescription: A dark, film-led opening pairs an agent-and-property moving image with a compact search control. A dense region selector and property feed quickly hand off into distinct cinematic chapters, then a development strip, media and technology capabilities, press features, and a long multi-path contact close. White listing intervals create contrast against dark story scenes. The source's people, properties, prices, statistics, words, badges, logos, video, and trademarked identity remain source-only. The transferable idea is a media-led brokerage whose search, market reach, and supporting disciplines are expressed as separate scenes.

heroGeometry.alignment: centered headline over dark moving image with compact search below
heroGeometry.viewport: opening identifies the real-estate service and starts property discovery without a text wall

navigationGeometry.placement: thin top overlay over the opening scene
navigationGeometry.mobile: reduce top utility links to a touch-safe menu while preserving a direct search or contact action

typography.scale: large short headline, dense market labels, restrained explanatory copy

palette.ink: white on cinematic scenes and deep blue-black on light listing surfaces
palette.contrastIntent: strong scene contrast with readable labels and accessible search controls

imageTreatment.crop: full-width moving-image stills interrupted by precise listing crops
imageTreatment.focalPoint: preserve the principal residence or human subject and keep key text over quiet image regions

servicePresentation.interaction: searchable market taxonomy followed by property feed and distinct brokerage-discipline scenes

ctaPlacement.primary: find a property through the hero search
ctaPlacement.secondary: browse regions or contact an advisor
ctaPlacement.early: search overlay integrated into film hero

motion.library: native video or CSS with optional GSAP sequencing
motion.reducedMotion: poster still with fully visible search, labels, and links

mobileRecomposition.strategy: stacked media search and listing feed
rules: keep the first search control above the initial listing sequence
stack development and service scenes rather than shrinking desktop carousels
preserve legible property facts and tap-sized controls
provide a poster image when video or motion is unavailable

prohibitedPatterns: copying SERHANT. names, logos, video, people, properties, listing data, statistics, claims, or trademarks
reproducing the exact dark and electric-blue trade dress
making the page a generic card wall
allowing autoplay video to carry essential content
inventing agent credentials, market reach, sales totals, prices, or availability

requiredSignatureElements.description: A large media hero combines with an integrated property and location search.
Market selection leads into a property discovery feed rather than isolated generic service cards.
Supporting brokerage capabilities appear as separate media, technology, or development story chapters.

acceptanceChecks: The first viewport has a clear, working property-search or inquiry action.
Property discovery and business capabilities have distinct section treatments.
A still-image fallback communicates the opening if motion is disabled.
Client location, service scope, credentials, prices, and property facts come only from sealed client content.
At 390 px, no navigation, search, or listing information overflows horizontally.

review.notes: Official home and about pages confirm brokerage, property search, market, and supporting media/business divisions. Full-page desktop and mobile screenshots were inspected. Browser reported no broken content images; unresolved lazy image elements and non-blocking source JavaScript errors are recorded in the capture record.
